verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own Relay Proxy, a Go application that runs on your own infrastructure. It proxies the LaunchDarkly streaming connection to clients inside your organization's network, which covers keeping SDK traffic internal. The outage-resilience half (flags still served when LaunchDarkly is unreachable) is supported only by a community mention of "extra resiliency", not by first-party docs on caching or persistent-store behavior during vendor outages. missing for 10: documented offline/outage serving behavior (persistent store or cache when upstream is unreachable), hands-on corroboration of outage resilience, deployment/HA configuration details.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can run a relay/edge proxy so flags stay served when the vendor is unreachable and SDK traffic stays inside my network

citations.quote: a small Go application that runs on your own infrastructure. It connects to the LaunchDarkly streaming API and proxies that connection to clients
It connects to the LaunchDarkly streaming API and proxies that connection to clients within your organization’s network.
LaunchDarkly has an open source 'Relay' you can run in your own environment for extra resiliency.
